Dear all,
 Below is an R script which defines a simulator function for simulating distance sampling data for multiple primary periods, packaging it up into an unmarkedFrame and then fitting the hazard and half-normal detection models.
 THEN: some data are set to missing values and the models are refitted.
 
 This analysis seems to reliably produce an error in fitting the half-normal model (but not the hazard model).  I believe that there is an error within the half-normal likelihood function (you can look at the gdistsamp function simply by editing it and search on "nll" to see the likelihood definition).   I don't know whether there is really a problem with the hazard model or not but if someone wants to play with this script and try to produce consistent errors with that function then please do.
 
 I will give a free book to the first unmarked user who can identify the error in missing value handling which produces the error in the half-normal model.  
 The book will be this one:
http://www.amazon.com/Applied-Hierarchical-Modeling-Ecology-distribution/dp/0128013788/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1438204252&sr=8-1&keywords=kery+and+royle
 
regards,
andy
 
 
# A function for simulating open HDS data under a temporary emigration model
simHDSopen <- function(type="line", nsites = 100, mean.lam = 2,
beta.lam = 0, mean.sig = 1, beta.sig = 0, B = 3, discard0=TRUE, nreps=2, phi=0.7, nyears=5, beta.trend = 0){
# Function simulates hierarchical distance sampling data under either a
#   line (type = "line") or a point (type = "point") transect protocol.
# Simulates a LIST OF LISTS of individual observations.
#   element [[i]][[j]] is the individual observations for replicate j of year i
# Function arguments:
#   nsites: Number of sites (spatial replication)
#   alpha.lam (= log(mean.lambda)), beta.lam: intercept and
#      slope of log-linear regression of expected lambda
#      on a habitat covariate
#   alpha.sig (= log(mean.sigma)), beta.sig: intercept and
#      slope of log-linear regression of scale parameter of
#      half-normal detection function on wind speed
#   B: strip half width
#
#   more things here
#
#  
#  Note: for "point" the realized density is
#[(area of circle) /(area of  square)]*lambda
parmvec <- c(mean.lam, beta.lam, mean.sig, beta.sig, phi, beta.trend)
names(parmvec)<- c("mean.lam", "beta.lam", "mean.sig", "beta.sig", "phi", "beta.trend")

# Make a covariate
habitat <- rnorm(nsites)                    # habitat covariate
# covariate "wind" is replicate level covariate
# Simulate abundance model (Poisson GLM for M)
M <-lambda <- matrix(NA, nrow=nsites, ncol=nyears)
Na <- wind <- array(NA,dim=c(nsites,nreps,nyears))
Na.real <- array(0, dim =c(nsites,nreps,nyears))
for(i in 1:nyears){
lambda[,i] <- exp(log(mean.lam) + beta.lam*habitat + beta.trend*(i-nyears/2) )
# density per "square"
M[,i] <- rpois(nsites, lambda[,i])           # site-specific abundances
Na[,,i] <- matrix(rbinom(nsites*nreps, M[,i],phi), nrow=nsites, byrow=FALSE)
wind[,,i] <- runif(nsites*nreps, -2, 2)   # Wind covariate
}

# Detection probability model (site specific)
# this is now a 3-d array
sigma <- exp(log(mean.sig) + beta.sig*wind)

# Simulate observation model

## http://www.anderswallin.net/2009/05/uniform-random-points-in-a-circle-using-polar-coordinates/
outlist <-list()
for(yr in 1:nyears){

list.yr <-list()
for(rep in 1:nreps){
data <- NULL
for(i in 1:nsites){
  if(Na[i,rep,yr]==0){
    data <- rbind(data, c(i,NA,NA,NA,NA)) # save site, y=1, u1, u2, d
    next
  }
  if(type=="line"){
    # Simulation of distances, uniformly, for each ind. in pop.
    # note it piles up all M[i] guys on one side of the transect
    d <- runif(Na[i,rep,yr], 0, B)
    Na.real[i,rep,yr]<- sum(d<=B)
    p <- exp(-d *d / (2 * (sigma[i,rep,yr]^2)))
    # Determine if individuals are captured or not
    y <- rbinom(Na[i,rep,yr], 1, p)
    u1 <- u2 <- rep(NA, Na[i,rep,yr])   # coordinates (u,v)
    # Subset to "captured" individuals only
    d <- d[y==1]
    u1 <- u1[y==1]
    u2 <- u2[y==1]
    y <- y[y==1]
  }

  if(type=="point"){
    # Simulation data on a square
     u1 <- runif(Na[i,rep,yr], 0, 2*B)
     u2 <- runif(Na[i,rep,yr], 0, 2*B)
  if(1==1){
   angle <- runif(Na[i,rep,yr], 0, 360)
    dd<- B*sqrt(runif(Na[i,rep,yr],0,1))
    u1<- dd*cos(angle) + (B)
    u2<- dd*sin(angle) + (B)
 }
 
    d <- sqrt((u1-B)^2 + (u2-B)^2)
    Na.real[i,rep,yr]<- sum(d<= B)
 if(is.na(Na.real[i,rep,yr])) browser()
    p <- exp(-d *d / (2 * (sigma[i,rep,yr]^2)))
    # But we can only count individuals on a circle so we truncate p here
    pp <- ifelse(d < B, 1, 0) * p
    y <- rbinom(Na[i,rep,yr], 1, pp)  # Det./non-detection of each individual
cat("n : ", sum(y==1), fill=TRUE)
    # Subset to "captured" individuals only
    u1 <- u1[y==1]
    u2 <- u2[y==1]
    d <- d[y==1]
    y <- y[y==1]
  }

  # Compile things into a matrix and insert NA if no individuals were
  # captured at site i. Coordinates (u,v) are not used here.
  if(sum(y) > 0)
    data <- rbind(data, cbind(rep(i, sum(y)), y, u1, u2, d))
  else
    data <- rbind(data, c(i,NA,NA,NA,NA)) # make a row of missing data

  }
list.yr[[rep]]<- data
}
outlist[[yr]]<- list.yr
}
# Subset to sites at which individuals were captured. You may or may not
#  want to do this depending on how the model is formulated so be careful.
if(discard0)
  data <- data[!is.na(data[,2]),]
list(data=outlist, B=B, nsites=nsites, habitat=habitat, wind=wind, M.true= M, K=nreps,nyears=nyears,Na=Na, Na.real=Na.real,
  mean.lam=mean.lam, beta.lam=beta.lam, mean.sig=mean.sig, beta.sig=beta.sig, phi=phi, beta.trend=beta.trend, parms=parmvec )
}

 


# Obtain a temporary emigration data set
set.seed(1234)
str(tmp <- simHDSopen("point", nreps=7, nyears=5, nsites=100)  )
attach(tmp)
 
apply(tmp$M.true,2,sum)
 

 

# Define distance class information
delta <- 0.5
nD <- B%/%delta                 # Number of distance classes
midpt <- seq(delta/2, B, delta) # Mid-point of distance intervals

# Create the 4-d array
y4d <- array(0,dim=c(nsites, nD, K, nyears))
for(yr in 1:nyears){
  for(rep in 1:K){
    data <- tmp$data[[yr]][[rep]]
    site <- data[,1]
    dclass <- data[,"d"]%/%delta + 1
    ndclass <- B%/%delta
    dclass <- factor(dclass, levels= 1:ndclass)
    y4d[1:nsites,1:nD,rep,yr] <- table(site, dclass)
  }
}

 

y3d <- y4d[,,,1]

Yflat<- cbind(y3d[,,1],y3d[,,2],y3d[,,3])
breaks<- c(0, .5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3)*100

library(unmarked)

# Package into unmarked GDS data frame and inspect the data
umf <- unmarkedFrameGDS(y = Yflat, survey="point", unitsIn="m",
   dist.breaks=breaks, numPrimary = 3,
   siteCovs = data.frame(habitat))
str(umf)
summary(umf)

 

 


# hazard detection function
 fm0.haz <- gdistsamp(lambdaformula = ~1, phiformula = ~1, pformula = ~1,
   keyfun = "haz", output = "density", unitsOut = "ha",
   mixture = "P", K = 100, se = TRUE, data = umf )
# half-normal detection function: DOES NOT WORK
fm0.hn <- gdistsamp(lambdaformula = ~1, phiformula = ~1, pformula = ~1,
   keyfun = "halfnorm", output = "density", unitsOut = "ha",
   mixture = "P", K = 100, se = TRUE, data = umf )


# Create a new data set
Yflat.na<-Yflat
Yflat.na[100 , 7:12]<- NA

umfNA <- unmarkedFrameGDS(y = Yflat.na, survey="point", unitsIn="m",
   dist.breaks=breaks, numPrimary = 3,
   siteCovs = data.frame(habitat))
 


# hazard detection function
 fm0.haz <- gdistsamp(lambdaformula = ~1, phiformula = ~1, pformula = ~1,
   keyfun = "haz", output = "density", unitsOut = "ha",
   mixture = "P", K = 100, se = TRUE, data = umfNA )
# half-normal detection function
fm0.hn <- gdistsamp(lambdaformula = ~1, phiformula = ~1, pformula = ~1,
   keyfun = "halfnorm", output = "density", unitsOut = "ha",
   mixture = "P", K = 100, se = TRUE, data = umfNA , starts = c(-2.29, 0, 4) )

 


 


On Wed, Jul 29, 2015 at 4:44 PM, Jeffrey Royle <jar...@gmail.com> wrote:
hi all,
 
  I wish I could say exactly what is going on but I'm afraid I don't know.  For quite awhile I thought the result was due to poor starting values but I'm somewhat convinced now that there must be a problem with internal handling of missing values. We've noticed this in a few different applications where you can fix the problem either by restricting to numPrimary=1 or by setting NA to 0 (or by deleting observations with NA).
 
 My problem right now is that the result is not very predictable and I haven't had time to do a definitive study to try to narrow down potential causes.
 
 I will work on developing a simulation study of this during the summer and see if I can reliable generate the error which should help fix the problem....
 
regards
andy
 

On Wed, Jul 29, 2015 at 4:34 PM, Sarah Thompson <thom...@umn.edu> wrote:
Hey all, I'm getting similar errors with gdistsamp, so just checking in if Andy found any potential solutions or targeted specific issues for gdistsamp.

gdistsamp will work for my data if I only use the first round of surveys (i.e. numPrimary = 1) -- this works great, even on pretty complicated models, with any of the keyfuns or distributions.

When I add one additional round of surveys (with about 10% of the second surveys being not conducted/NAs), it generally won't work. I've messed around a bunch trying to figure out what the issue is. Adding start values, changing the keyfun, or distribution doesn't seem to help in my case. This is on a null model, no covariates.

I generally get this warning:

Warning message:
In gdistsamp(~1, ~1, ~1, data = umfGDS, keyfun = "hazard", output = "density",  :
  Hessian is singular. Try using fewer covariates and supplying starting values.

If I try to keep multiple rounds of surveys:
- It works if I replace NAs with 0s (which is obviously a silly thing to do, but does indicate NAs are likely? the issue). 
- Sometimes, it works when I change the default optim method ("CG" worked this round, but no others, and took a really long time). However, I'm not entirely sure of the repercussions of this switch, and I doubt this "trick" will continue to work when I try to put in covariates or survey round #3 with about 50% NAs.

Thought I'd just check in here for hints before I am relegated to bugs :) 

Thanks!
Sarah Thompson

Hi All,

I'm trying to use gdistsamp to model density of small prey along transects. I have 5 survey periods that I would like to include as yearlySiteCovs to estimate survey-specific phi, and a lot of missing data because many sites were not sampled all 5 times. Initially I was using the command "formatDistData" to convert my data into the format required for gdistsamp. My models all ran fine and a half-normal key function best fit the data. However, I didn't realize that all of the NAs in my data were being converted to 0s when I used formatDistData, making it look like I had surveyed way more sights than I had, and that I had found nothing. I think I have my data entered correctly now,  with the NAs, but now the only model I can get to run is an exponential key function, which is not recommended in distance modeling. Half-normal and hazard rate functions both give me errors. I've tried using starting values from the exponential function in the other two, but I get the same errors.  Does anyone have any ideas why my models won't run with the NAs added? Andy;
I think I see what's causing the error. In gdistsamp, in the half-normal nll function, you assign -Inf as the default value in matrix mn. I assume you are thinking that exp(-Inf) = 0. However, when the function gets to line:
g[i, ] <- exp(rowSums(mn))
rowSums() produces a value of 0 for the rows with -Inf. This then causes zeros in matrix g, which causes an attempt to calculate log(0) in line:
-sum(log(ll))

When I changed the line:
mn <- matrix(-Inf, lk, T)
to:
mn <- matrix(0, lk, T)
The function ran and produced the results below:

>fm0.hn <- gdistsamp_fn_eds(lambdaformula = ~1, phiformula = ~1, pformula = ~1,
+                        keyfun = "halfnorm", output = "density", unitsOut = "ha",
+                        mixture = "P", K = 100, se = TRUE, data = umfNA , starts = c(-2.29, 0, 4) )
> fm0.hn

Call:
gdistsamp_fn_eds(lambdaformula = ~1, phiformula = ~1, pformula = ~1, 
    data = umfNA, keyfun = "halfnorm", output = "density", unitsOut = "ha", 
    mixture = "P", K = 100, starts = c(-2.29, 0, 4), se = TRUE)

Detection:

AIC: 548.1805
>
I  think using 0 instead of -Inf will be OK, since you handle cases where all replicates have NA's with the line:
if (all(naflag[i, t, ])) next

Eric

#   B: strip half width

Na <- wind <- array(NA,dim=c(nsites,nreps,nyears))
Na.real <- array(0, dim =c(nsites,nreps,nyears))
for(i in 1:nyears){
lambda[,i] <- exp(log(mean.lam) + beta.lam*habitat + beta.trend*(i-nyears/2) )
# density per "square"
M[,i] <- rpois(nsites, lambda[,i])           # site-specific abundances
Na[,,i] <- matrix(rbinom(nsites*nreps, M[,i],phi), nrow=nsites, byrow=FALSE)
wind[,,i] <- runif(nsites*nreps, -2, 2)   # Wind covariate
}

# Detection probability model (site specific)
# this is now a 3-d array
sigma <- exp(log(mean.sig) + beta.sig*wind)

# Simulate observation model

## http://www.anderswallin.net/2009/05/uniform-random-points-in-a-circle-using-polar-coordinates/
outlist <-list()
for(yr in 1:nyears){

list.yr <-list()
for(rep in 1:nreps){
data <- NULL
for(i in 1:nsites){
  if(Na[i,rep,yr]==0){
    data <- rbind(data, c(i,NA,NA,NA,NA)) # save site, y=1, u1, u2, d
    next
  }
  if(type=="line"){
    # Simulation of distances, uniformly, for each ind. in pop.
    # note it piles up all M[i] guys on one side of the transect
    d <- runif(Na[i,rep,yr], 0, B)
    Na.real[i,rep,yr]<- sum(d<=B)
    p <- exp(-d *d / (2 * (sigma[i,rep,yr]^2)))
    # Determine if individuals are captured or not
    y <- rbinom(Na[i,rep,yr], 1, p)
    u1 <- u2 <- rep(NA, Na[i,rep,yr])   # coordinates (u,v)
    # Subset to "captured" individuals only
    d <- d[y==1]
    u1 <- u1[y==1]
    u2 <- u2[y==1]
    y <- y[y==1]
  }

  if(type=="point"){
    # Simulation data on a square
     u1 <- runif(Na[i,rep,yr], 0, 2*B)
     u2 <- runif(Na[i,rep,yr], 0, 2*B)
  if(1==1){

    dd<- B*sqrt(runif(Na[i,rep,yr],0,1))
    u1<- dd*cos(angle) + (B)
    u2<- dd*sin(angle) + (B)
 }

# A function for simulating open HDS data under a temporary emigration model
simHDSopen <- function(type="line", nsites = 100, mean.lam = 2,
beta.lam = 0, mean.sig = 1, beta.sig = 0, B = 3, discard0=TRUE, nreps=2, phi=0.7, nyears=5, beta.trend = 0){
# Function simulates hierarchical distance sampling data under either a
#   line (type = "line") or a point (type = "point") transect protocol.
# Simulates a LIST OF LISTS of individual observations.
#   element [[i]][[j]] is the individual observations for replicate j of year i
# Function arguments:
#   nsites: Number of sites (spatial replication)
#   alpha.lam (= log(mean.lambda)), beta.lam: intercept and
#      slope of log-linear regression of expected lambda
#      on a habitat covariate
#   alpha.sig (= log(mean.sigma)), beta.sig: intercept and
#      slope of log-linear regression of scale parameter of
#      half-normal detection function on wind speed
#   B: strip half width
#
#   more things here
#
#  
#  Note: for "point" the realized density is
#[(area of circle) /(area of  square)]*lambda
parmvec <- c(mean.lam, beta.lam, mean.sig, beta.sig, phi, beta.trend)
names(parmvec)<- c("mean.lam", "beta.lam", "mean.sig", "beta.sig", "phi", "beta.trend")

# Make a covariate
habitat <- rnorm(nsites)                    # habitat covariate
# covariate "wind" is replicate level covariate
# Simulate abundance model (Poisson GLM for M)
M <-lambda <- matrix(NA, nrow=nsites, ncol=nyears)
Na <- wind <- array(NA,dim=c(nsites,nreps,nyears))
Na.real <- array(0, dim =c(nsites,nreps,nyears))
for(i in 1:nyears){
lambda[,i] <- exp(log(mean.lam) + beta.lam*habitat + beta.trend*(i-nyears/2) )
# density per "square"
M[,i] <- rpois(nsites, lambda[,i])           # site-specific abundances
Na[,,i] <- matrix(rbinom(nsites*nreps, M[,i],phi), nrow=nsites, byrow=FALSE)
wind[,,i] <- runif(nsites*nreps, -2, 2)   # Wind covariate
}

# Detection probability model (site specific)
# this is now a 3-d array
sigma <- exp(log(mean.sig) + beta.sig*wind)

# Simulate observation model

## http://www.anderswallin.net/2009/05/uniform-random-points-in-a-circle-using-polar-coordinates/
outlist <-list()
for(yr in 1:nyears){

list.yr <-list()
for(rep in 1:nreps){
data <- NULL
for(i in 1:nsites){
  if(Na[i,rep,yr]==0){
    data <- rbind(data, c(i,NA,NA,NA,NA)) # save site, y=1, u1, u2, d
    next
  }
  if(type=="line"){
    # Simulation of distances, uniformly, for each ind. in pop.
    # note it piles up all M[i] guys on one side of the transect
    d <- runif(Na[i,rep,yr], 0, B)
    Na.real[i,rep,yr]<- sum(d<=B)
    p <- exp(-d *d / (2 * (sigma[i,rep,yr]^2)))
    # Determine if individuals are captured or not
    y <- rbinom(Na[i,rep,yr], 1, p)
    u1 <- u2 <- rep(NA, Na[i,rep,yr])   # coordinates (u,v)
    # Subset to "captured" individuals only
    d <- d[y==1]
    u1 <- u1[y==1]
    u2 <- u2[y==1]
    y <- y[y==1]
  }

  if(type=="point"){
    # Simulation data on a square
     u1 <- runif(Na[i,rep,yr], 0, 2*B)
     u2 <- runif(Na[i,rep,yr], 0, 2*B)
  if(1==1){
   angle <- runif(Na[i,rep,yr], 0, 360)
    dd<- B*sqrt(runif(Na[i,rep,yr],0,1))
    u1<- dd*cos(angle) + (B)
    u2<- dd*sin(angle) + (B)
 }
 
    d <- sqrt((u1-B)^2 + (u2-B)^2)
    Na.real[i,rep,yr]<- sum(d<= B)
 if(is.na(Na.real[i,rep,yr])) browser()
    p <- exp(-d *d / (2 * (sigma[i,rep,yr]^2)))
    # But we can only count individuals on a circle so we truncate p here
    pp <- ifelse(d < B, 1, 0) * p
    y <- rbinom(Na[i,rep,yr], 1, pp)  # Det./non-detection of each individual
cat("n : ", sum(y==1), fill=TRUE)
    # Subset to "captured" individuals only
    u1 <- u1[y==1]
    u2 <- u2[y==1]
    d <- d[y==1]
    y <- y[y==1]
  }

  # Compile things into a matrix and insert NA if no individuals were
  # captured at site i. Coordinates (u,v) are not used here.
  if(sum(y) > 0)
    data <- rbind(data, cbind(rep(i, sum(y)), y, u1, u2, d))
  else
    data <- rbind(data, c(i,NA,NA,NA,NA)) # make a row of missing data

  }
list.yr[[rep]]<- data
}
outlist[[yr]]<- list.yr
}
# Subset to sites at which individuals were captured. You may or may not
#  want to do this depending on how the model is formulated so be careful.
if(discard0)
  data <- data[!is.na(data[,2]),]
list(data=outlist, B=B, nsites=nsites, habitat=habitat, wind=wind, M.true= M, K=nreps,nyears=nyears,Na=Na, Na.real=Na.real,
  mean.lam=mean.lam, beta.lam=beta.lam, mean.sig=mean.sig, beta.sig=beta.sig, phi=phi, beta.trend=beta.trend, parms=parmvec )
}

 


# Obtain a temporary emigration data set
set.seed(1234)
str(tmp <- simHDSopen("point", nreps=7, nyears=5, nsites=100)  )
attach(tmp)
 
apply(tmp$M.true,2,sum)
 

 

# Define distance class information

nD <- B%/%delta                 # Number of distance classes
midpt <- seq(delta/2, B, delta) # Mid-point of distance intervals

# Create the 4-d array
y4d <- array(0,dim=c(nsites, nD, K, nyears))
for(yr in 1:nyears){

    data <- tmp$data[[yr]][[rep]]

    dclass <- factor(dclass, levels= 1:ndclass)
    y4d[1:nsites,1:nD,rep,yr] <- table(site, dclass)
  }
}

 

y3d <- y4d[,,,1]

Yflat<- cbind(y3d[,,1],y3d[,,2],y3d[,,3])
breaks<- c(0, .5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3)*100

library(unmarked)

# Package into unmarked GDS data frame and inspect the data
umf <- unmarkedFrameGDS(y = Yflat, survey="point", unitsIn="m",
   dist.breaks=breaks, numPrimary = 3,
   siteCovs = data.frame(habitat))
str(umf)
summary(umf)

 

 


# hazard detection function
 fm0.haz <- gdistsamp(lambdaformula = ~1, phiformula = ~1, pformula = ~1,
   keyfun = "haz", output = "density", unitsOut = "ha",
   mixture = "P", K = 100, se = TRUE, data = umf )
# half-normal detection function: DOES NOT WORK
fm0.hn <- gdistsamp(lambdaformula = ~1, phiformula = ~1, pformula = ~1,
   keyfun = "halfnorm", output = "density", unitsOut = "ha",
   mixture = "P", K = 100, se = TRUE, data = umf )


# Create a new data set
Yflat.na<-Yflat
Yflat.na[100 , 7:12]<- NA

umfNA <- unmarkedFrameGDS(y = Yflat.na, survey="point", unitsIn="m",
   dist.breaks=breaks, numPrimary = 3,
   siteCovs = data.frame(habitat))
 


# hazard detection function
 fm0.haz <- gdistsamp(lambdaformula = ~1, phiformula = ~1, pformula = ~1,
   keyfun = "haz", output = "density", unitsOut = "ha",
   mixture = "P", K = 100, se = TRUE, data = umfNA )
# half-normal detection function
fm0.hn <- gdistsamp(lambdaformula = ~1, phiformula = ~1, pformula = ~1,
   keyfun = "halfnorm", output = "density", unitsOut = "ha",
   mixture = "P", K = 100, se = TRUE, data = umfNA , starts = c(-2.29, 0, 4) )

 My problem right now is that the result is not very predictable and I haven't had time to do a definitive study to try to narrow down potential causes.
 
 I will work on developing a simulation study of this during the summer and see if I can reliable generate the error which should help fix the problem....
 
regards
andy
